justification: Changes how the rules route picks a council's rules and PDF links for every property. Wrong, it serves another council's plan or none; the change replaces a name pattern with the stored key.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any former_council value the page sent in the 30-address audit maps to a key other than the stored source_council, or the route goes back to a document-name pattern or a bare toLowerCase lookup.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Putting back `const councilSlug = filters.former_council.toLowerCase();` printed 'Tests: 1 failed, 17 passed, 18 total'. Restored: 18 passed.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Production, 2026-10-11: for each of 18 source_council values, rows selected by `document_id ILIKE pattern` and by `source_council = key` were counted: identical for every real council; the pattern additionally caught 2,420 Ashfield rows for 'inner_west' and 22 Marrickville 'part9_p35_parramatta_rd' rows for Parramatta. The audit captures show the page sending 'City of Sydney' (0 chapter_pdf_urls) and 'city_of_parramatta' (0 rules).

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions.source_council (18 values) and dcp_chapter_registry.council use the same lowercase underscore keys; city_of_sydney registry rows carry r2_public_pdf_url for schedules, section 3 and section 4.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The route assumed the page sends a slug. It sends Planning Portal names ('City of Sydney', 'Leichhardt') or page-made slugs ('city_of_parramatta'), and three lookups each converted them differently.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One small pure function in lib, used at the six lookups; the old COUNCIL_DOC_PATTERNS map and councilToDocPattern are removed because nothing else used them.

functions.name: councilKey
functions.input: The former council name the page sends: a Planning Portal name, a page-built slug, or nothing at all.
functions.output: The lowercase underscore key used as source_council and dcp_chapter_registry.council, with two aliases.
functions.if_none: Null for an empty name; the route only adds the council filter when a former council was sent.

break_it.scenario: A council whose stored key differs from its normalised Portal name (another alias like city_of_parramatta).
break_it.what_happens: That council shows 0 rules -- visible as an empty list, not wrong rules.
break_it.how: The audit's 15 real inputs are pinned in the test; the served-answer audit capture flags any address served 0 rules.

break_it.scenario: Rows whose source_council is NULL but whose document_id named the council.
break_it.what_happens: Those rules would quietly stop showing on the page.
break_it.how: Counted on production: 0 such rows for any council (pattern and key select identical sets).
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE is_current AND v2_is_actionable AND source_council IS NULL AND document_id ILIKE '%_DCP%'

break_it.scenario: An Inner West house with no former council (inner_west fallback).
break_it.what_happens: Was shown Ashfield's whole DCP; now shows only Inner West LEP rows.
break_it.how: Intended: no former council means no council DCP can be chosen; the LEP land gate (DQ-140) still applies.

mutation_analysis: Forced: restoring toLowerCase for the registry turned the suite red. Removing the city_of_parramatta alias fails its case; a councilKey that returned its input unchanged fails 'City of Sydney' and 'Ku-ring-gai'.
residual_risk: Other routes (app/api/provisions/route.ts and similar) were not changed in this PR; only the route the assessment page uses. A council added later with an unusual Portal name needs an alias -- it fails visibly (0 rules), not silently wrong.

post_merge.manual_verify: After deploy: load 6 Eccles Street Ermington and 2 Hawksley Street Waterloo on /assessment; Parramatta rules appear and Sydney rules carry PDF links.
